title: Protocol for Human Monocyte-to-Macrophage Polarization Using Tumor Conditioned Media
author: George, Georgouli, et al.
materials: BD FACS CANTO II flow cytometer

steps.title: Obtain PBMCs from buffy coats
steps.instruction: Acquire peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from anonymized human buffy coats supplied by NHSBT (Tooting, London, UK). Whole blood or blood cones may be used as alternatives.

steps.title: Dilute buffy coat 1:2 with PBS
steps.instruction: Dilute 50 mL of buffy coat 1:2 with PBS (−/− CaCl₂/MgCl₂; Gibco) at room temperature; e.g., mix 15 mL buffy coat with 30 mL PBS.

steps.title: Layer diluted buffy coat onto Lymphoprep
steps.instruction: Using a 50 mL Falcon tube, gently layer 30 mL of the diluted buffy coat on top of 15 mL Lymphoprep (STEMCELL Technologies; room temperature) by slowly pipetting to the side of the tube, tilting the tube at a 45° angle for the first few milliliters.

steps.title: Centrifuge density gradient at 800 g
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube in a swinging‑bucket rotor at 800 × g for 30 min at room temperature (15 °C–23 °C) with maximum acceleration and brake set to 0.

steps.title: Collect PBMCs and transfer to PBS
steps.instruction: Collect the white‑interface PBMC layer with a disposable Pasteur pipette and transfer into a 50 mL Falcon tube containing fresh PBS (−/− CaCl₂/MgCl₂).

steps.title: Wash PBMCs at 200 g for 10 min
steps.instruction: Top up the tube to 50 mL with PBS and centrifuge at 200 × g for 10 min at room temperature with normal brake; discard supernatant.

steps.title: Repeat PBMC wash and resuspend
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 50 mL PBS (−/− CaCl₂/MgCl₂) and repeat the 200 × g, 10 min wash as above.

steps.title: Count live cells with Trypan Blue
steps.instruction: Determine live cell number using a hemocytometer with Trypan Blue. Prepare a 1:10 dilution (e.g., 10 µL PBMC suspension + 20 µL Trypan Blue + 70 µL PBS), mix well, and count.

steps.title: Centrifuge cells at 300 g for 10 min
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300 × g for 10 min at room temperature with normal brake.

steps.title: Resuspend PBMCs in MACS buffer with CD14 beads
steps.instruction: Resuspend PBMCs in pre‑cooled MACS buffer (PBS −/− CaCl₂/MgCl₂, 0.5 % FBS, 2 mM EDTA) at 1 × 10⁷ cells per 80 µL and add 20 µL CD14 microbeads (Miltenyi). Keep MACS buffer on ice.

steps.title: Incubate labeling mixture at 4 °C 15 min
steps.instruction: Mix the cell suspension thoroughly and incubate for 15 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Add MACS buffer and centrifuge at 300 g
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL MACS buffer per 1 × 10⁷ PBMCs (e.g., 30 mL for 30 × 10⁷ cells) and centrifuge at 300 × g for 10 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Resuspend cells at 10⁸ cells/mL in MACS buffer
steps.instruction: After centrifugation, resuspend the pellet in MACS buffer to a final density of 1 × 10⁸ cells/mL.

steps.title: Filter cell suspension through 70 µm strainer
steps.instruction: Pass the cell suspension through a 70 µm cell strainer to homogenize the mixture and prevent column blockage.

steps.title: Prepare LS column in magnetic separator
steps.instruction: Place the LS column in the Midi‑MACS separator where a magnetic field is applied.

steps.title: Pre‑soak LS column with MACS buffer
steps.instruction: Add 3 mL MACS buffer to the LS column to pre‑soak it. Avoid introducing air bubbles and never let the buffer run dry.

steps.title: Apply labeled cells to LS column
steps.instruction: Apply the magnetically labeled cell suspension onto the LS column; unlabeled (CD14⁻) cells will flow through into a 15 mL Falcon tube.

steps.title: Wash column three times with MACS buffer
steps.instruction: Perform three washes by adding 3 mL MACS buffer to the column each time; add new buffer only when the reservoir is nearly empty.

steps.title: Elute CD14⁺ cells with fresh MACS buffer
steps.instruction: After the washes are clear, add 5 mL fresh MACS buffer onto the LS column and push the plunger down firmly to elute the retained CD14⁺ cell fraction.

steps.title: Count and plate CD14⁺ cells in RPMI complete
steps.instruction: Count the eluted CD14⁺ cells, resuspend at 1 × 10⁶ cells/mL in RPMI complete medium (10 % FBS, 1 % Penicillin‑Streptomycin, 2 mM Glutamine), plate in standard tissue‑culture‑treated multiwell plates, and incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂. Optional: repeat steps 14‑19 on a second LS column to increase purity.

steps.title: Keep isolated CD14⁺ cells on ice
steps.instruction: Transfer a portion (<10⁶ cells) of the isolated CD14⁺ monocytes to ice and keep them there for the duration of the flow‑cytometry preparation.

steps.title: Centrifuge cells at 300 g 5 min 4 °C
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the iced cells at 300 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash once with FACS buffer and centrifuge
steps.instruction: Wash the pellet once with FACS buffer (PBS−/−, 1 % BSA, 2 mM EDTA, 0.1 % NaN₃) and centrifuge again at 300 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Block Fc receptors in FACS buffer 10 min RT
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 100 µL FACS buffer containing 5 µL FcR blocking solution (BioLegend) and incubate for 10 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Wash and centrifuge after blocking
steps.instruction: Top up with FACS buffer, centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min at 4 °C, and discard supernatant.

steps.title: Stain with anti‑CD14 antibody (1/20) 100 µL
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 100 µL FACS buffer containing anti‑human CD14 PerCP/Cy5.5 antibody diluted 1/20; vortex gently to mix.

steps.title: Incubate staining mixture 30 min 4 °C in dark
steps.instruction: Incubate the stained cells for 30 min at 4 °C protected from light.

steps.title: Wash with FACS buffer and centrifuge
steps.instruction: Wash the cells with FACS buffer and centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Repeat wash step
steps.instruction: Perform a second identical wash with FACS buffer and centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Resuspend in DAPI solution (5 µg/mL) 300‑500 µL
steps.instruction: Resuspend the final pellet in 300–500 µL DAPI solution (5 µg/mL in FACS buffer). To make 5 mL of this buffer, dilute 5 µL of a 5 mg/mL DAPI stock into 5 mL FACS buffer.

steps.title: Prepare compensation beads with CD14 antibody
steps.instruction: Add one drop each of ‘blank’ and ‘anti‑mouse’ Igκ beads (Miltenyi) to 100 µL FACS buffer, add 5 µL CD14 antibody (same dilution as staining), vortex gently, then top up to 300–500 µL FACS buffer.

steps.title: Transfer samples to FACS tubes for acquisition
steps.instruction: Transfer the stained cell suspensions and compensation bead preparations to FACS tubes.

steps.title: Acquire data on flow cytometer
steps.instruction: Run the samples on a BD FACS CANTO II flow cytometer and collect data.
